name: Mercury
facts: The closest planet to the Sun.
Robotic spacecraft have flown past and orbited it. No people have been there.
whyNot: Too close to the Sun: crews would face extreme heat and radiation.

name: Venus
facts: Thick clouds trap heat, making its surface the hottest of any planet.
Robotic landers have reached the surface, but did not last long.
whyNot: Its surface heat and crushing air pressure would destroy a crewed lander.

name: Earth
facts: Our home. Every mission starts from here and is guided by Mission Control here.

name: The Moon
facts: People have walked here: twelve astronauts landed during the Apollo missions, from 1969 to 1972.
NASA's Artemis program plans to send astronauts back.

name: Mars
facts: Robots explore it today, like NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers.
No people have been there yet. NASA is preparing for future crewed missions.

name: Jupiter
facts: The biggest planet. It is a gas giant, so there is no solid ground to land on.
Robotic spacecraft have studied it from orbit.
whyNot: No surface to land on, and very strong radiation around it.

name: Saturn
facts: Famous for its rings, made of ice and rock.
A gas giant, studied up close by robotic spacecraft.
whyNot: No surface to land on, and it is very far away.

name: Uranus
facts: An ice giant that spins tipped over on its side.
Only one spacecraft has flown past it.
whyNot: Too far: a trip would take many years.

name: Neptune
facts: The farthest planet from the Sun, with very strong winds.
Only one spacecraft has flown past it.
whyNot: Too far: a trip would take many years.
